description: Labelled test headlines for Headline to Market. expectedOutcome: 'market' means the tool should produce a settleable market draft; 'unresolvable' means it should refuse with a reason (expected rejection).

cases.headline: Bengaluru Metro Blue Line extension opens to the public on December 1
cases.snippet: BMRCL confirmed that the Yellow Line... sorry, Blue Line extension between RT Nagar and Airport will be inaugurated on December 1, according to officials familiar with the timeline.
cases.why: Concrete event, definite date, named authority (BMRCL) can settle it.

cases.headline: IMD predicts heavy rainfall in Bengaluru tomorrow
cases.snippet: The India Meteorological Department has issued a yellow alert for Bengaluru Urban, forecasting heavy rainfall in the next 24 hours.
cases.why: IMD is a named source with published data that settles YES/NO.

cases.headline: RBI to raise repo rate at next MPC meeting
cases.snippet: Analysts split on whether the Reserve Bank of India will hold or hike at the upcoming Monetary Policy Committee meeting.
cases.why: Binary, dated event; RBI's policy statement is the named source.

cases.headline: Will Bengaluru traffic improve?
cases.why: The real-world bad example: no metric, no source, no close condition. Expected rejection.

cases.headline: Is the new Namma Metro station art the most beautiful in India?
cases.snippet: Residents are debating the murals installed at the new metro stations.
cases.why: Purely subjective; no authority can settle a taste judgement. Expected rejection.

cases.headline: Did India win the 2011 ODI World Cup?
cases.why: Already settled in the past; opening a market on it is meaningless. Expected rejection.

cases.headline: Something exciting happened in tech yesterday
cases.why: No entity, no event, no verifiable condition. Expected rejection.

cases.headline: AI to replace most journalism jobs within five years
cases.why: Hard case: 'most' has no measurable threshold, no named source reports this, and the claim is unfalsifiable. Expected rejection.

cases.headline: Bengaluru IT corridor rents to rise sharply this year
cases.why: Hard case: 'rise sharply' has no measurable threshold, and no single public source tracks IT-corridor rents authoritatively. Expected rejection.
